text:
devon (acme-corp): Hi team — after we moved to Private VPC with the customer's default-deny egress policy, their calls to our KMS are returning 403s and the embeddings endpoint latency is huge. Billing shows a spike. Need urgent help, customer blocked.

tara (support): Thanks, devon. Can you paste the exact error from our side and any customer-side firewall policy?

devon (acme-corp): From our logs: `error: kms.request failed status=403, body="AccessDenied"`. Customer sent their egress ACL: only allow DNS (53) and HTTPS to internal registry, everything else denied. They expected us to talk to KMS via NAT but it looks blocked.

maria (sec): 403 to KMS usually means the request hit KMS but the key policy or principal failed, or we're stripping auth headers at the proxy. But with strict egress, packets might be getting NATed to a proxy with different IP, could break KMS allowlist.

jon (infra): Quick checks: 1) Is the outbound NAT gateway configured for the private deployment? 2) Is the egress using a TLS-inspecting proxy that rewrites SNI / client cert?

devon (acme-corp): They confirmed NAT gateway exists but they route 0.0.0.0/0 via a firewall that only allows a few destinations. No TLS inspection. They showed a tcpdump from their NAT showing SYN->RST for <kms-host>:443. I attached a snippet.

devon (acme-corp): ```
15:03:21.123456 IP 10.0.5.12.54321 > kms.external.example.com.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0
15:03:21.123789 IP kms.external.example.com.443 > 10.0.5.12.54321: Flags [R], seq 0, win 0, length 0
```

maria (sec): That R suggests the KMS endpoint is refusing based on source IP or TLS fingerprint. Could be HSM/KMS configured to only accept requests from known IPs and the customer's NAT is ephemeral.

tara (support): Also flag: billing spike — could be repeated retries. If requests immediately get a 403, the client might be retrying or falling back and generating extra tokens. Can we see client retry behavior in our logs?

jon (infra): I see a pattern: our agent retries 3x with exponential backoff but not backoff jitter; combined with a large pool of clients that could explain token thrash. We should rate-limit retries for 4xx.

sec-oncall: Assigning sec-oncall. Need timeline and whether this is affecting other customers.

audit-bot: New incident record created: INC-2026-3479 (private-vpc-kms-403) — assigned to sec-oncall and infra.

sec-oncall: On it. Maria, can you confirm if our control plane is including any identifying source IPs that need to be allowlisted? Also need HSM/KMS audit logs (call source, key id).

maria (sec): Control plane doesn't expose customer NAT IPs to KMS; the calls originate from the customer's VPC via their NAT. We can ask the customer to provide the public IPs observed. For HSM/KMS audit logs, request from our KMS provider: need timestamp range + key ids.

devon (acme-corp): Customer provided NAT range: 3.144.12.0/28 (single elastic IP rotated weekly). They say they rotate but we can get the current one.

jon (infra): Temporary mitigation: ask customer to allowlist current EIP for their NAT on the KMS key policy, and relax firewall to allow outbound to kms.external.example.com:443. Also disable aggressive retries on agent side ASAP.

tara (support): Repro steps for our ops playbook: 1) Enable debug on agent; 2) Run single request to embeddings endpoint; 3) Capture outbound IP at customer NAT; 4) Check KMS request/response headers in agent debug logs.

devon (acme-corp): Attached agent debug log: `Authorization: Bearer <redacted>` sent, got 403. No `x-request-id` returned.

maria (sec): Two action items from sec: - Confirm if customer is using an IP allowlist on KMS key policy (likely) - If so, advise temporary allowlist and plan for stable IP egress (elastic IP not rotated during rollout)

jon (infra): I'll open a config patch to change retry policy for 4xx to not retry and add jitter. Pushing canary in 10m.

ops-runbook: Note for runbook update: add a VPC-private-kms troubleshooting section — include commands to curl KMS endpoint from a bastion and how to capture NAT EIP. Example: `curl -v https://kms.external.example.com:443 -I` and `curl https://ifconfig.me` to see public IP.

sec-oncall: Also, we need KMS/HSM provider audit logs for the window 2026-05-20T14:50Z -> 2026-05-20T15:20Z (approx). Maria, please request via provider support and include requestor email.

maria (sec): Request opened with KMS provider support, ticket 87412. Asked for TLS handshake logs and key policy denies.

devon (acme-corp): Customer rolled back egress to allowlist our KMS and reports success — auth fixed, latency back to normal. They still want us to recommend a long-term pattern for stable egress IPs.

tara (support): Closing the immediate blocker. Follow-ups: 1) Update docs with stable egress patterns for Private deployments 2) Add retry guard for 4xx 3) Add runbook snippet for NAT EIP capture and KMS allowlist steps

jon (infra): Can someone file a small RFC for supported egress architectures (nat gateway vs centralized proxy) and whether we support publishing expected IPs for customers to allowlist? I'll take infra-side of RFC.

maria (sec): I'll draft guidance for key policies and rotating EIP best practices; include risks of dynamic IPs and recommended use of customer-managed NAT with static EIP.

sec-oncall: Thanks all. Marking incident RESOLVED for customer unblock. Keeping the RFC and runbook follow-ups as tasks. :white_check_mark:

tara (support): FYI billing spike: support confirmed retries accounted for ~12k extra token operations during the window. Finance notified to apply a customer credit.

devon (acme-corp): Thanks team — appreciate the quick turnaround.

maria (sec): Pushing runbook patch shortly.

jon (infra): Canary deployed for retry backoff change. Monitoring.

ops-runbook: Runbook updated (PR #329) with NAT troubleshooting section and sample tcpdump snippet.
